title: Research Scientist / Research Engineer, Automated Safety
location: Cambridge, MA USA; London, UK; San Francisco, CA USA
description:
Your Impact at LILA

We're building a talent-dense, high-agency AI safety team at Lila that will engage all core teams within the organization (science, model training, lab integration, etc.), to identify and mitigate risks from scientific superintelligence while retaining the core scientific discovery capabilities of the stack. The initial focus of this team will be to build and implement a bespoke safety strategy for Lila, tailored to its specific goals and deployment strategies. This will involve technical safety strategy development, broader ecosystem engagement, safety-focused evaluations, safety systems to mitigate risks, and a research agenda that explores longer-term needs such as oversight of superintelligent scientific systems.

As scientific AI systems become more capable and autonomous, their safety assessment and safeguards must develop alongside them. At Lila Sciences, you will help build the research methods and tools that make this possible, so that more and more decision-enablers can be automated safely. This will move us closer to the vision of a safety and security apparatus that is robust to a fully autonomous scientific engine.

Your initial focus will be misuse: developing flexible and automated red-teaming approaches that test safety-relevant scientific capabilities and the robustness of safeguards. You will also contribute to safety automation beyond red teaming, helping the team evaluate, monitor and respond to risks across increasingly autonomous scientific workflows. You will own reusable research methods and assessment tools, working with mitigation engineers who implement protective mechanisms. We welcome Research Scientists and Research Engineers; responsibilities can span or evolve between the two profiles.

What You'll Be Building

  • Develop and run capability evaluations of scientific models, agents and tool-mediated workflows (including simulated lab environments), working with domain experts to make tests scientifically meaningful.
  • Create methods or systems that explore diverse failure modes, adapt tests as evidence emerges and support systematic investigation beyond fixed benchmarks.
  • Build reproducible experiments and evaluation tools that capture relevant behavior, outcomes and the evidence needed to interpret findings.
  • Measure the quality and coverage of automated assessments, including failure cases in the evaluators themselves.
  • Develop broader safety automation, across threat model management, evidence triage, regression testing, monitoring workflows or tools that help researchers assess and respond to risks.
  • Collaborate with risk researchers and mitigation engineers to translate findings into improved assessments and safeguards, and verify whether those changes work.

What You'll Need to Succeed

  • Strong empirical judgment, practical programming ability and experience working with modern AI systems.
  • The ability to investigate ambiguous failures, design informative comparisons and communicate limitations clearly.
  • An interest in scientific misuse risks and the ability to collaborate productively with domain specialists.
  • For the Research Scientist profile: evidence of selecting valuable research questions, developing or adapting methods, and designing experiments that yield defensible conclusions. You should be able to prototype and test your ideas.
  • For the Research Engineer profile: evidence of building reliable research software, evaluation infrastructure or agent systems that enable reproducible experiments and efficient iteration. You should be able to contribute to experimental design and interpretation.

Bonus Points For

  • Automated red teaming, adversarial testing or evaluation-method research.
  • Scientific AI, tool-using agents, laboratory automation or other complex environments.
  • Experience with safety monitoring, model-based evaluators or scalable experimental infrastructure.

Compensation

We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

U.S. Benefits. Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.

International Benefits. Full-time employees outside the U.S. receive a comprehensive benefits program tailored to their region. USD salary ranges apply only to U.S.-based positions; international salaries are set to local market.

title: Associate Director of Project Services
description:
Position Summary

The Associate Director of Project Services is responsible for leading and executing the successful launch of new products, process improvements and technology transfers, with a strong emphasis on project management and risk mitigation. This role manages both Project Managers and a technical team, ensuring projects are delivered on time, within budget, and to required quality standards. This position acts as the primary interface between cross-functional teams and Outside Sales for launch execution, overseeing risk analysis, line trials, and initial production activities.

The Associate Director of Project Services heads cross-functional meetings between R&I, Quality, Production, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Outside Sales. They are responsible for development of OKRs that drive performance and evaluation based on those metrics.

Responsibilities and Essential Duties

  • Ensure the safe and consistent execution of launches.

  • Develop and implement robust risk assessments for product launches, identifying technical and operational risks and mitigation plans.

  • Collaborate with Sales to ensure communication with customers.

Technical Skills Required

  • Comprehensive understanding of product development, product launch and product supply chains.

  • Strong understanding of stability and compatibility protocols.
  • Advanced knowledge of production equipment and associated batching and filling capabilities.

  • Strong oral and written communication skills.

  • 5+ years of experience managing direct reports.
  • Experience managing cross-functional teams.

Physical Requirements

  • Regularly sit, stand, and walk for extended periods of time.
  • Ability to sit, balance, climb, stand, bend, squat, squeeze, kneel, turn, crouch, stoop repeatedly.

  • Frequent exposure to varying temperatures, loud noises, heavy machinery, fumes, airborne particles, electrical, chemicals, and moving parts.

title: Chief Advancement Officer
description:
Position Summary
The Chief Advancement Officer (CAO) is a key member of the Executive Team responsible for advancing Beech Brook’s mission through integrated oversight of development, marketing/communications, and external relations. Reporting to the CEO and working in close collaboration with Beech Brook’s Board President and Development Chair, the CAO leads strategy and execution for fundraising, communications, and brand positioning to drive organizational growth, visibility, and long-term sustainability.
An immediate priority for this role will be leading donor development and fundraising efforts associated with the organization’s Family Center’s move to Midtown. Beech Brook will be mounting a campaign to support the build out, growth and sustainability of the Family Center’s new location. In addition, Beech Brook is celebrating its 175th anniversary beginning in January 2027. While planning is underway with current staff and Board leadership, the CAO will be responsible for oversight of the anniversary activities, through the lens of development, and aligning those activities with the Family Center campaign and ongoing development needs.
The CAO directly supervises the Director of Development, Director of Marketing & Communications and Development Associate, providing leadership, direction, and accountability across all advancement functions.
The position will be primarily located at Beech Brook’s Granger Road headquarters with some time spent at the Family Center in Midtown. Beech Brook offers some flexibility to work from home at the organization’s discretion.
Key Responsibilities
  • Cultivating and expanding partnership opportunities, especially in Midtown.
  • Provide strategic leadership and oversight of Development and Marketing departments, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and growth objectives.
  • Lead comprehensive advancement strategy, including fundraising, donor engagement, communications, and brand development.
  • Design and lead a multi-year plan that aligns fundraising and marketing/communications opportunities for the Family Center campaign, 175th anniversary, and ongoing contributed income needs.
  • Drive donor development efforts at the highest level, including identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of major and transformational gifts.
  • Maintain donor data integrity and reporting.
  • Provide direct supervision, coaching, and performance management for advancement team leadership, including Director of Development, Director of Marketing & Communications and Development Associate. [JC1]
  • Partner closely with the CEO, Board leadership, and Executive Team on organizational strategy, external relations, and long-term planning.
  • Serve as a primary liaison to the Board of Directors on advancement- and marketing/communications-related matters.
  • Actively participate in Board committees, including:
    • Governance Committee
    • Development Committee
    • Leadership Development and Nominating Committee
    • Marketing Committee
  • Support board engagement, recruitment, and development of future leadership.
  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with key stakeholders, including major donors, foundations, corporate partners, and community leaders.
  • Represent the organization publicly to enhance visibility, partnerships, and philanthropic support, including serving as a media spokesperson
Qualifications
  • Significant leadership experience in nonprofit advancement, fundraising, or external affairs. Knowledge of the Northeast Ohio philanthropic community preferred.
  • Demonstrated success leading major campaigns and securing principal and major gifts, preferably in complex human services or healthcare-related organizations.
  • Proven success in leading integrated development and marketing/communications functions.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively with executive leadership and boards.
  • Strong strategic thinking, communication, and relationship-building skills.
Organizational Culture
Beech Brook, the recipient of the Plain Dealer/Cleveland .com Top Workplace award for 7 years in a row is a trauma-informed care organization committed to improving outcomes for children and families. Leaders are expected to model integrity, collaboration, and a deep commitment to the agency’s mission.

title: Data & AI Manager — Revenue Growth Management
description:
Revenue Growth Management only works when Sales, Marketing and Commercial Excellence are pulling the same lever at the same time. Most Consumer & Retail organizations don't have one person who can sit across all three and turn pricing, promotion and mix into a strategy everyone actually commits to.

You want to be that person for our clients: the subject matter expert and trusted partner Sales, Marketing and ComEx bring into the room when RGM strategy needs to be built, not just reported on.

As a Data & AI Manager and RGM subject matter expert in our Consumer & Retail practice, you will be the key stakeholder client teams across Sales, Marketing and Commercial Excellence rely on to shape their Revenue Growth Management strategy. You won't run a delivery team — you will own the thinking and the relationship: framing the strategy, challenging assumptions, and briefing Data Engineers, Data Scientists and Solution Architects so what gets built actually holds up commercially.

You won't be building the pricing models yourself, but you will need to be fluent enough in elasticity, trade spend and mix economics to shape a strategy, defend it across functions, and know when the data is telling a different story than the client expects.

Responsibilities

  • Be the client's RGM subject matter expert: build trusted, ongoing relationships with Sales, Marketing and Commercial Excellence stakeholders as the go-to expert on pricing, promotion and mix strategy
  • Shape the strategy: facilitate discovery across Sales, Marketing and ComEx, and translate competing commercial priorities into one clear, prioritized RGM strategy
  • Build the business case: size RGM opportunities, structure the investment case, and secure sign-off from client leadership on the roadmap and its sequencing
  • Brief the builders: define requirements and commercial guardrails for Data Engineers, Data Scientists and Solution Architects and hold the solution accountable to the strategy
  • Own value tracking: make sure the strategy lands as adopted ways of working across Sales, Marketing and ComEx, not a one-off recommendation
  • Grow the practice: contribute to RGM proposals and presales, and build EPAM's point of view on Revenue Growth Management

Requirements

  • Deep RGM expertise: hands-on experience shaping Revenue Growth Management strategy — pricing, promotion, trade spend or mix — built in-industry or through sustained consulting with CPG/FMCG, retail or wholesale clients, with concrete, quantified business impact
  • Trusted partner across the commercial organization: a proven ability to build credibility and long-term relationships across Sales, Marketing and Commercial Excellence, not just one function
  • Consulting craft: structured problem-solving, executive-level communication, and comfort building alignment across stakeholders with different priorities
  • Data and AI literate: able to define data and modeling requirements, hold a substantive conversation with a data scientist or pricing analyst, and translate between commercial and technical audiences
  • End-to-end experience: from strategy through to delivery and adoption, with a clear, honest view of what worked and what didn't
  • Comfortable with ambiguity: takes ownership and drives a client to outcomes without waiting to be told what the answer is

Nice to have

  • Familiarity with RGM/pricing platforms (e.g., Revionics, Pricefx, Blue Yonder, Impact Analytics, PROS) or major cloud platforms (Azure, GCP, AWS)

title: Creative Art Director
description:
About WPP Production

We are WPP Production - the unified global production company that brings together all of WPP's content producers, studios and craft experts into one connected organisation. We combine world-class human craft with next generation technology to originate, design, and deliver multi-channel content systems at scale. Built for borderless collaboration and powered by deep craft expertise, we are the production engine designed for today's always on, AI driven marketing world.

WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. At WPP Production, you’ll help shape the future of content production at a truly global scale. title: Security Engineer - GRC Federal Frameworks

description:

  • Experience implementing and maintaining security compliance frameworks and cloud security controls.
  • Expert-level knowledge in at least one of the following domains: DoD Cloud Computing SRG IL5/IL6, FedRAMP Class D. and/or NIST 800-171/CMMC.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and translation skills, with experience influencing cross-functional teams and communicating risks to leadership.
  • Experience with commercial compliance programs (e.g., ISO 27001, ISO 42001, SOC 2, NIST CSF, NIST 800-53, or similar compliance framework is a plus.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

title: Quality Program Manager, YouTube Trust and Safety

title: Site Sanitation Supervisor
description:
At Ecowize North America, we’re more than a sanitation company — we’re protecting the

food supply and supporting the health of millions every single day. Our work matters,

and so do the people who make it happen. We invest in our people, give them the tools to succeed, and create opportunities for growth. As a Sanitation Site Supervisor, you’ll play a key role in leading teams, ensuring safe and effective cleaning practices, and helping us deliver on our promise of excellence to our clients.

About the Role: Sanitation Site Supervisor

The Sanitation Site Supervisor leads daily sanitation operations at a client facility that

runs multiple shifts, seven days a week. You’ll work closely with your team before,

during, and after sanitation shifts — ensuring the site is ready, safety protocols are

followed, and food safety standards are met.

This is a hands-on leadership role where you’ll coach frontline employees, manage

sanitation processes, oversee shift readiness, and serve as the point of contact with both

client management and regulatory inspectors.

What You’ll Do

Lead Sanitation Teams: Supervise and support sanitation employees to ensure proper staffing, safe practices, and effective cleaning processes.

Ensure Shift Readiness: Coordinate with client maintenance teams pre-shift, verify lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures, and confirm equipment access.

Drive Safety & Food Safety: Reinforce PPE use, GMPs, SSOPs, and HAZCOMM

practices; ensure compliance with USDA/FDA requirements.

Inspect & Approve Work: Conduct equipment inspections before, during, and after

sanitation to ensure readiness for production.

Partner with Inspectors & Clients: Accompany USDA/QA inspectors during pre-op

inspections and maintain strong communication with client leadership.

Manage Documentation: Complete and maintain sanitation logs, deficiency reports, training records, and time/attendance records.

Enforce Standards: Apply company policies consistently, including progressive discipline when needed.

Adapt to Needs: Adjust staffing to cover short crews, manage budgets responsibly, and drive continuous improvement in sanitation effectiveness.

What You Bring

· Experience: 2–3 years in sanitation leadership within food processing (USDA/FDA environment required).

· Sanitation Knowledge: Strong understanding of GMPs, SSOPs, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), PPE, and chemical handling.

· Supervisory Skills: Ability to lead, coach, and develop hourly teams in a fast-paced environment.

· Bilingual Preferred: English and Spanish.

· Adaptability: Willingness to work varied shifts (days, nights, weekends, holidays) and in all plant conditions (hot, cold, wet, loud).

Key Competencies for Success

Leadership: You set clear expectations, motivate your team, and lead by example.

Accountability: You take ownership of results, documentation, and compliance.

Collaboration: You work effectively with peers, client staff, inspectors, and regulators.

Attention to Detail: You ensure cleaning standards, safety procedures, and documentation are never compromised.

Resilience: You remain dependable, professional, and composed in challenging environments.

What We Value

Partnership: Building trust with clients and teammates.

Excellence: Delivering on commitments with precision and care.

Integrity: Doing the right thing, always.

The Details

Job Type: Full-time

Schedule: 8- to 10-hour shifts; days, nights, weekends, holidays as needed

Work Environment: Hands-on work in food plant settings; requires physical

stamina and use of PPE

Travel: Minimal, site-based role

What You’ll Get

· Competitive pay

· Health, dental, and vision insurance

· 401(k) with company match

· Paid time off and holidays

· Professional development support

· Relocation assistance (where applicable)

· Retirement plan options

Your Future Starts Here

At Ecowize, we don’t just provide sanitation services — we build careers. As a Sanitation

Site Supervisor, you’ll lead with purpose, grow with support, and make an impact every

day.

title: Sap ABAP Consultant
description:
Job Title: Senior SAP ABAP Consultant

Experience: 5 - 8 Years

Location: Jharsuguda


Key Responsibilities

• Technical Design & Development: Analyze functional specifications and design,

develop, test, and debug complex ABAP programs, reports, interfaces, conversions,

enhancements, and forms (RICEFW objects).

• SAP S/4HANA Expertise: Develop and adapt code for SAP S/4HANA, utilizing Core

Data Services (CDS) views, AMDP (ABAP Managed Database Procedures), and

OData services. Understand and adhere to the code restrictions and best practices

for SAP HANA.

• Interface & Integration: Design and build efficient and stable interfaces using RFC,

BAPI, IDocs, ALE, and Web Services (SOAP/REST). Experience with SAP PI/PO or

CPI is a strong plus.

• Enhancement & Modification: Utilize appropriate enhancement techniques (User

Exits, BAdIs, Enhancement Spots) and modification strategies (SPDD/SPAU) to

customize SAP standard functionality to meet business needs.

• Performance Tuning: Analyze and optimize the performance of existing and new

ABAP code for SAP HANA, including code pushdown techniques and effective use

of OpenSQL.

• Forms & Output Management: Develop and maintain print forms using SAP Script,

Smart Forms, and Adobe Forms (Adobe Interactive Forms or Adobe LiveCycle

Designer).

• Workflow (Optional but valued): Develop and maintain SAP workflow rules and

processes to automate business tasks.

• Collaboration: Work closely with SAP Functional Consultants (MM, SD, FI/CO, PP,

etc.) to understand business processes and provide optimal technical solutions.


• Documentation & Standards: Create and maintain detailed technical

documentation. Adhere to internal coding standards, best practices, and change

management procedures.

• Support & Troubleshooting: Provide technical support for production issues,

perform root cause analysis, and implement effective solutions in a timely manner.


Required Qualifications & Skills

• Experience: 5-8 years of hands-on experience in SAP ABAP development.

• Education: Bachelors degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.

• Technical Proficiency:

  • Core ABAP: Mastery of Object-Oriented ABAP (OOPS), ALV reporting, Dialog

Programming (Module Pools), and Data Dictionary.

  • RICEFW: Proven experience in developing the full spectrum of RICEFW objects.
  • Interfaces: Strong experience with RFC, BAPI, IDoc, and ALE configuration and

programming.

  • Enhancements: Expert knowledge of User Exits, Customer Exits, BAdIs, and

Enhancement Framework.

  • Forms: Solid experience with at least two of the following: SAPscript, Smart Forms,

Adobe Forms.

• S/4HANA Readiness: Hands-on development experience with CDS Views, AMDP,

and OData Services is mandatory.

• Performance: Strong understanding of ABAP performance analysis and tuning tools

(e.g., SAT, ST12).

• Methodologies: Familiarity with Agile and Scrum methodologies.

• Problem-Solving: Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.

• Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to

explain complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications (Nice-to-Have)

• Experience with one full lifecycle SAP S/4HANA implementation or migration project.

• Knowledge of SAP Fiori development principles and UI5.

• Experience with SAP BTP (Business Technology Platform) and ABAP Steampunk

(ABAP in the Cloud).

• Familiarity with integration tools like SAP Process Integration (PI/PO) or Cloud

Platform Integration (CPI).

• Exposure to SAP modules such as FI, CO, MM, SD, or PP to better understand the

functional context.

• Knowledge of version control systems like Git.

title: NGM - Lead Permitting Specialist
description:
Position Description:

Would you like to have a career with a collaborative, diverse, and dynamic mining company? We have an exciting opportunity for you!

Our people division is growing, and we are looking for a Lead Permitting Specialist with our Environmental team. This position supports the continued effectiveness and advancement of Nevada Gold Mines’ environmental permitting program across assigned operations and projects. This role provides leadership for complex permitting initiatives, NEPA analyses, major project authorizations, and regulatory engagement activities. The position serves as a technical and strategic leader within the Environment & Natural Resources team, helping to manage permitting risks, support project execution, mentor permitting professionals, and strengthen the organization’s future leadership pipeline.

At Nevada Gold Mines, our vision is to be the world’s most valued gold mining business by finding, developing, and operating the best assets with the best people. We are committed to a safe work environment sending every person home safe and healthy every day and leaving a sustainable legacy on our host communities.

Responsibilities:

  • Accountable for the overall effectiveness and execution of the NEPA permitting program for assigned operation(s).
  • Lead permitting strategies for major mining, infrastructure, exploration, closure, and operational projects.
  • Develop permitting roadmaps aligned with mine plans, business objectives, and project schedules.
  • Identify permitting risks, constraints, and opportunities early and recommend solutions.
  • Ensure State and Federal permit applications, Plans of Operations, NEPA documents, supporting technical studies, and associated regulatory deliverables are complete, technically sound, and legally defensible.
  • Direct baseline studies and technical investigations supporting permitting activities.
  • Coordinate multidisciplinary technical inputs including wildlife, hydrology, geochemistry, air quality, water quality, cultural resources, reclamation, and socioeconomic resources.
  • Review technical reports and environmental analyses for quality and defensibility.
  • Integrate permitting requirements into project planning and life-of-mine strategies.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact with federal, state, tribal, and local regulatory agencies for assigned projects.
  • Lead applicable agency meetings, site visits, technical reviews, and project presentations.
  • Coordinate responses to agency comments and requests for information.
  • Build and maintain effective working relationships with regulatory agencies and stakeholders.
  • Provide functional leadership, technical mentorship, and guidance to permitting specialists and support environmental professionals across the organization.
  • Promote consistency, quality, and best practices across permitting activities and project execution.
  • Support employee development through coaching, training, and succession planning.
  • Coordinate and prioritize permitting resources across assigned projects and provide day-to-day leadership support for direct reports.
  • Partner with site environmental teams to facilitate the effective transition of permitted projects into site environmental compliance and operational management programs.

  • Develop scopes of work, budgets, schedules, and contracting strategies for permitting projects and studies.

title: Field Construction Technician
description:
Position Title: Field Construction Technician


Rate of Pay: $23.00 to $39.00 hourly DOE

Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, 401k, flexible spending account, paid sick leave and paid time off, parental leave, quarterly performance bonus, training, career growth and education reimbursement programs.


Ziply Fiber is a local internet service provider dedicated to elevating the connected lives of the communities we serve. We offer the fastest home internet in the nation, a refreshingly great customer experience, and affordable plans that put customers in charge.


As our state-of-the-art fiber network expands, so does our need for team members who can help us grow and realize our goals.


Our Company Values:


  • Genuinely Caring: We treat customers and colleagues like neighbors, with empathy and full attention.
  • Empowering You: We help customers choose what is best for them, and we support employees in implementing new ideas and solutions.
  • Innovation and Improvement: We constantly seek ways to improve how we serve customers and each other.
  • Earning Your Trust: We build trust through clear, honest, human communication.


Job Summary

The Field Construction Technician installs, repairs, and maintains Ziply Fiber's fiber-to-the-premises network from the outside plant through to the customer's home or business. The role combines installations, fusion splicing, and trouble ticket repair with outside plant fiber construction, testing, and network maintenance. The Field Construction Technician diagnoses and repairs technical issues within the network or at a customer's home, with occasional assistance, while delivering outstanding customer service as a brand ambassador of Ziply Fiber within our communities.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

The Essential Duties and Responsibilities listed below are a range of duties performed by the employee and not intended to reflect all duties performed.


Fiber Construction, Splicing, and Testing

· Perform fusion splicing of fiber drop cables at customer premises, ensuring proper fiber preparation and splice enclosure management.

· Prep, splice, and maintain fiber optic cables in aerial, underground, and indoor settings.

· Assist with single fusion and mass fusion splicing on high-count fiber optic cables (24-ribbon and above) in outside plant environments.

· Utilize OTDR, PON power meters, and VFLs to test fiber, troubleshoot, and identify network issues.


Installation, Repair, and Service Delivery

· Provision, install, and troubleshoot internet and VoIP services.

· Diagnose and repair technical issues within the network infrastructure or at the customer's home.

· Place NIDs and non-buried drops, perform cross-connect work, install and maintain inside wiring for residential and business broadband service.

· Utilize test equipment to install products and isolate trouble effectively.

· Read and understand service orders and trouble tickets and use handheld dispatch devices and Ziply Fiber's internal dispatch programs to complete assignments.

· Record customer information, light levels, OTDR readings, and internet speed readings on every work order.

· Maintain proper work cleanliness, attic safety, drilling safety, and proper wall drops.

· Communicate effectively with customers.


Network Maintenance, Documentation, and Safety

· Assist with network maintenance and equipment turn-up as needed, including putting generators at the huts.

· Support the preventive maintenance program by rebuilding aerial, buried, and underground cables.

· Read and interpret outside plant drawings, splicing schematics, blueprints, and engineering documents.

· Assist with mid-sheath entries, bonding and grounding fibers, and maintaining existing plant.

· Adhere to OSHA, NESC, and NEC safety standards, including in-vehicle safety and work zone setups.

· Participate in on-call rotations to ensure network health and respond to network outages (24/7 on-call capability).


Other Duties

· Performs other duties as required to support the business and evolving organization.


Required Qualifications:

· High school diploma or GED.

· One (1) year of outside plant fiber-splicing experience, including single-fiber fusion splicing, mass fusion (ribbon) splicing on high-count fiber-optic cables (24-ribbon and above), and fiber testing and troubleshooting using OTDRs, PON power meters, and VFLs.

· Good safety record.

· Knowledge of first aid and CPR.

· Strong communication skills, problem-solving abilities, and customer service orientation.

· Must have and maintain a valid driver’s license, auto insurance, and satisfactory driving record.

· Must complete a pre-employment drug screening.


Preferred Qualifications:

· Experience with fiber optic construction and maintenance, sealed plant repair, and/or operation of heavy equipment.

· Experience with PON access equipment (e.g., Nokia, Adtran, Calix).

· Basic AC/DC theory.


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

· Ability to learn and understand basic routing, switching, and fiber-optic transmission and equipment concepts.

· Ability to understand outdoor engineering and outside plant prints, network layouts, designs, and symbols.

· Ability to climb, work aloft, and work in close spaces, including attics and crawl spaces.

· Ability to remain calm in high stress situations and demonstrate good judgment.

· Ability to interpret written, oral, and diagnostic form instructions over a short period of time and execute those instructions with accuracy.

· Ability to read and understand road maps, discern street signs, and address numbers.

· Ability to operate equipment to perform the essential functions of the job (i.e., fusion and mechanical splicing tools, OTDR, PON power meter, VFL, attenuation test sets, locator, handheld dispatch device, computer/laptop, telephone, company vehicle, trailers, aerial devices, and various hand and power tools, shovel and rake).

· Ability to be unaffected by flashing lights and strobes.

· Ability to always maintain a professional manner and appearance.

· Ability to drive on behalf of the company in a safe and responsible manner.


Work Authorization

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the US for any employer. Sponsorship is not available for this position.


Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


Work requires standing and walking continuously, frequent fine manipulation and carrying, and occasional sitting and keyboarding, along with bending, stooping, and kneeling for prolonged periods. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. The ability to work in tight spaces, climb poles and ladders, work in aerial buckets, and lift heavy equipment up to 75 pounds. Travel approximately 10% of the time.


Work Environment

Work is performed outdoors on job sites in residential areas and commercial buildings, with exposure to weather conditions including extreme heat, rain, and cold. Includes work in attics and crawl spaces, occasional work in underground vaults and manholes, aloft in a bucket, and some indoor work near electrical equipment.


At all times, Ziply Fiber must be your primary employer. Unless otherwise prohibited by law, employees may not hold outside employment nor be self-employed without obtaining approval in writing from Ziply Fiber. In holding outside employment or self-employment, employees should ensure that participation does not conflict with responsibilities to Ziply Fiber or its business interests.


Diverse Workforce / EEO:

Ziply Fiber is an equal opportunity employer. Ziply Fiber will consider all qualified candidates regardless of race, color, religion, national origin, gender, age, marital status, sexual orientation, veteran status, and the presence of a non-job-related handicap or disability or any other legally protected status.


Ziply Fiber requires a pre-employment background check as conditions of employment. Ziply Fiber may require a pre-employment drug screening.


Ziply Fiber is a drug free workplace.

title: Senior Director of Graduate and International Admissions
description:
LIM College - The Business of Fashion & Lifestyle is currently seeking candidates for the position of Senior Director of Graduate and International Admissions

GENERAL DESCRIPTION:
Founded in 1939 and located in midtown Manhattan, LIM College is focused on the global business of fashion and lifestyle. Offering master’s, bachelor’s, and associate degree programs, LIM prepares students forcareer success via an immersive approach grounded in real-world experience and learning by doing required internships. LIM College’s commitment to excellence in business education ensures graduates are sought after by a wide range of employers, as evidenced by a Career Outcomes Rate of 96% for the Class of 2022. Alumni excel throughout all areas of fashion and lifestyle and have gone on to work for companies such as Chanel, Gucci, Alexander McQueen, Ross Stores, The Financial
Times, Ulta Beauty, Google, Saks Fifth Avenue, Cannabis Creative, and The National Football League.

POSITION PURPOSE:
The Senior Director of Graduate and International Admissions provides strategic leadership for the recruitment, admission, and enrollment of graduate and international students for the College’s on-campus programs, and supports the recruitment of students for the College’s online graduate programs. Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Enrollment Management and Student Success, the position directs the work of the Graduate and International Admissions staff, develops and executes recruitment strategies to achieve enrollment goals, and provides the coaching, support, and feedback staff need to succeed.
The position may serve as or supervise the College’s Principal Designated School Official (PDSO) under the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) and holds primary institutional responsibility for compliance with U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) regulations governing F-1 international students. The position supervises the College’s Designated School Official(s) (DSO), maintains the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) and the College’s Form I-17 certification, and serves as the institution’s principal liaison to SEVP, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), and related federal agencies.
The position works closely with the Vice President of Admissions and Enrollment Operations and the Senior Director of Admissions Recruitment, and partners with Academic Affairs, graduate program directors, the Registrar, Marketing and Communications, Student Financial Services, Student Affairs, and Career Services. The position represents the division on matters related to graduate and international enrollment as delegated and provides regular reports and updates to senior leadership.

SALARY RANGE: $110,000 - $120,000/Annually

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND BASIC DUTIES
Graduate and International Admissions Leadership
  • Direct the day-to-day operations of Graduate and International Admissions, including prospect and applicant management, application review and admission decisions, and yield activities, in alignment with College admission standards and enrollment goals.
  • Supervise, train, and evaluate assigned staff; set clear performance expectations and key performance indicators; conduct regular individual meetings; and coach and mentor staff to strengthen individual and team performance.
  • Apply a data-informed approach to decision-making; monitor funnel performance; and prepare weekly, monthly, and annual reports and analyses on graduate and international enrollment for senior leadership.
  • Analyze market and enrollment trends to identify opportunities for growth and efficiency, and contribute graduate and international data to annual admissions and assessment reporting.
Graduate Recruitment
  • Develop and execute an annual graduate recruitment plan, in partnership with the Senior Vice President and the Senior Director of Admissions Recruitment, with defined goals, markets, budget, and tactics for on-campus graduate programs.
  • Partner with graduate program directors and faculty on admission standards, applicant review, and yield engagement.
  • Build and manage graduate pipelines through LIM undergraduate and alumni channels, corporate and industry partnerships, and graduate information sessions and events.
  • Coordinate with Student Financial Services on graduate scholarships, assistantships, and financial aid communication to support yield.
  • Support recruitment for online graduate programs in coordination with the Director of Online Admissions, including program-specific messaging, applicant review as assigned, and referral of prospective students best served by online programs.
International Recruitment
  • Develop and execute an international recruitment strategy, including market prioritization, international travel, and virtual engagement.
  • Manage education agent relationships, including selection, agreements, training, and performance monitoring, consistent with College policy and recognized industry standards.
  • Support the development of articulation and pathway partnerships with international institutions and partners.
  • Establish and maintain standards for international credential evaluation and English-language proficiency in collaboration with Academic Affairs.
  • Collaborate with Marketing and Communications on international-facing communications and materials.
International Student Compliance (PDSO)
  • Serve as the College’s Principal Designated School Official, with institutional authority and responsibility under 8 CFR 214.3 for SEVP certification and F-1 regulatory compliance.
  • Maintain the College’s Form I-17, including timely updates for material changes and successful completion of SEVP recertification on the required cycle.
  • Nominate, add, and remove DSOs in SEVIS; supervise the DSO(s); and ensure completion of SEVP-required training and continuing regulatory education.
  • Oversee the issuance of Forms I-20 and ensure accurate and timely SEVIS reporting of all required student events within federally mandated timeframes.
  • Adjudicate and advise on F-1 benefits and requests, including Curricular Practical Training (CPT), Optional Practical Training (OPT) and STEM OPT extensions, reduced course load, program extensions, transfers, reinstatement, and travel endorsements.
  • Develop and maintain institutional policies and procedures for F-1 admission, enrollment, and record-keeping; conduct periodic internal audits of SEVIS data and student files; and lead the College’s response to SEVP site visits, audits, and inquiries.
  • Ensure the integrity of international student data across SEVIS, the CRM, and the student information system, and the retention of records in accordance with federal requirements.
  • Monitor federal rulemaking and SEVP guidance; assess institutional impact; brief senior leadership and campus partners; and serve as the College’s subject-matter expert on F-1 regulations for faculty and staff.
  • Coordinate international student immigration check-in, orientation, and ongoing immigration advising.
Collaboration and Divisional Responsibilities
  • Serve as liaison to Academic Affairs, the Registrar, Student Financial Services, Academic Advising, Student Affairs, Career Services, and Marketing and Communications to ensure that graduate and international processes are communicated and executed according to College policy.
  • Foster a culture in which faculty and staff understand and value their role in the recruitment and retention of graduate and international students.
  • Work with enrollment consultants and vendor partners as assigned, serving as project manager where appropriate.
  • Represent the division on matters related to graduate and international enrollment as delegated by the Senior Vice President; serve on committees and task forces as requested; and perform other duties as assigned.
PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENTS
  • Graduate and international applicant and enrollment goals are met or exceeded, and online graduate recruitment targets are supported.
  • SEVP certification and the Form I-17 are maintained in good standing, and recertification is completed on schedule without adverse findings.
  • SEVIS records are accurate and complete, and all required reporting is submitted within mandated timeframes.
  • DSO(s) are properly designated, trained, and supervised, and institutional policies and procedures for F-1 compliance are current and documented.
  • Recruitment plans, travel, and events are informed by data; staff expectations are clearly articulated; and staff are engaged and performing to potential.
  • Reports are accurate and delivered on time, and senior leadership is appropriately informed of progress toward goals.
  • Effective communication and coordination are maintained with campus partners, and applicants are informed of all processes, procedures, and deadlines.

REQUIREMENTS: The person selected will have the following qualifications:

EDUCATION/CERTIFICATION:
  • Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree preferred.
REQUIRED EXPERIENCE:
  • Seven or more years of progressive admissions or enrollment management experience, including at least three years in a supervisory capacity. U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident, as required by federal regulation (8 CFR 214.3(l)) to serve as a PDSO/DSO, and the ability to obtain and maintain PDSO designation. Progressive experience in admissions or enrollment management with demonstrated success in achieving recruitment goals. Working knowledge of graduate and international admissions practices. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and CRM systems (Slate preferred).
PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:
  • Prior DSO or PDSO experience with working knowledge of SEVIS, F-1 regulations, and SEVP policy guidance. Graduate and international recruitment experience, including education agent management and international travel. Experience with J-1 regulations (RO/ARO), NAFSA training, or SEVIS-integration platforms. Proficiency in a second language.
SKILLS:
  • Strategic, analytical, and data-driven; strong written and verbal communication and presentation skills; cross-cultural competence; sound judgment and discretion in handling confidential and federally regulated information; project management and organizational skills; ability to travel domestically and internationally and to work occasional evenings and weekends.

WORK PERKS:
  • College Closed for Summer Fridays
  • Tuition Remission or Tuition Exchange
  • 6 Weeks of Paid Holidays
  • Birthday Day to Celebrate your Birthday
  • 2-4 weeks of vacation based on longevity; 7 sick days annually
  • Medical, Dental, Vision, Employee Assistance, 401K etc.

title: Summer Internship - Mechanical Engineering
description:
If you are searching for the best new ideas and share our vision, join us as a ”. This is what you need to know:

title: Finish Shop Lead
description:
Purpose

The Finish Shop Lead provides dedicated frontline leadership within the Finish Shop, directing the daily application of coatings and finishes to aircraft cabinetry and interior components for custom V/VVIP aircraft. The role coordinates daily finishing operations, provides quality oversight of finish work, and improves efficiency within the finishing process, while personally performing advanced spray application and finish work.

This position reports to the Finish Shop Supervisor and serves as the primary point of coordination between the finish shop crew, supervision, and adjacent production departments to support productivity, quality, employee development, and the on-time, airworthy re-delivery of aircraft.

Essential Job Functions

Finish Shop Leadership & Coordination

• Assign, schedule, and coordinate daily finishing tasks among finish shop personnel based on work orders, production plans, and re-delivery milestones.

• Plan and sequence finish work, booth time, and cure cycles to minimize bottlenecks, idle time, and rework.

• Conduct pre-shift safety briefings and shift handoffs, communicating task status, cure schedules, open items, and known hazards to incoming personnel.

• Provide hands-on technical direction, coaching, and on-the-job training in surface preparation, spray technique, color matching, and defect correction.

• Provide input to the Finish Shop Supervisor on crew performance, training needs, and staffing; promptly escalate personnel, safety, and quality concerns.

Finishing & Coating Application

• Perform advanced spray application of primers, sealers, stains, basecoats, and topcoats to aircraft cabinetry, veneers, and composite or honeycomb interior components in accordance with engineering specifications, finish schedules, and customer-approved samples.

• Perform and oversee surface preparation, including sanding, filling, grain filling, and masking, to achieve the specified finish quality.

• Mix, reduce, and catalyze coating materials in accordance with manufacturer technical data sheets, observing pot life, flash, and cure requirements.

• Perform color matching and verify color, sheen, and gloss against customer-approved samples and engineering-supplied data.

• Perform final finish work, including wet sanding, rubbing out, buffing, and polishing, to meet V/VVIP finish standards.

Quality, Compliance & Documentation

• Inspect finish work at defined stages; investigate finish defects such as orange peel, runs, solvent pop, fisheyes, blushing, and adhesion failure, determine the cause, and direct correction.

• Participate in quality audits and lead root cause corrective action (RCCA) on recurring finish defects in coordination with Quality.

• Perform documentation procedures and sign-offs in accordance with the Repair Station Quality Manual (RSQM) and respective task requirements; review crew documentation for accuracy and completeness before submission to Quality.

• Perform and verify proper tagging of finished components, parts, and panels, and ensure appropriate handling and storage to protect finished surfaces (including racks by aircraft).

• Enforce safety, hazardous material, and spray-finishing practices, including required PPE and respiratory protection, booth operation, and chemical handling and storage in accordance with Safety Data Sheets; maintain good housekeeping across the Finish Shop.

Materials, Equipment & Continuous Improvement

• Monitor coating and consumable inventory; initiate material orders and manage shelf life, batch tracking, and first-in, first-out (FIFO) rotation.

• Ensure spray guns, pumps, booths, filters, and other finishing equipment are properly cleaned, maintained, and returned to proper storage after use.

• Identify and implement process improvements that reduce rework, material waste, and cycle time.

• Maintain close and frequent communication with the Finish Shop Supervisor, Production Control, the Cabinet Shop, and Quality, reporting progress and any roadblocks that could impact re-delivery; deal with customers in a cordial, respectful, and professional manner.

• Take part in any required training as determined by the company, which may include advanced coating technologies, leadership skills, problem-solving and root cause corrective action methodologies, continuous improvement, and customer quality requirements.

Requirements

Required

• High school diploma or equivalent (GED).

• 5+ years of experience in spray application and surface finishing of high-end wood, veneer, or composite products, such as custom V/VIP aircraft furnishings, yacht interiors, or architectural millwork.

• Working knowledge of complete coating systems and paint chemistry fundamentals.

• Demonstrated ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, technical specifications, and manufacturer technical data sheets.

• Demonstrated ability to direct, train, and coordinate the work of others in a production shop environment.

• Able to read, understand, and apply technical data, engineering drawings, Safety Data Sheets, and regulatory documentation in English, and to communicate clearly with crew members, coworkers, and supervisors, including during safety briefings, crew coordination, and shift handoffs, to perform the essential functions of the position safely.

• Able to wear required PPE, including respiratory protection, and to complete the respirator medical evaluation and fit testing required under 29 C.F.R. § 1910.134.

• Must report for assignment with a personal set of standard trade-specific tools.

Preferred

• 5+ years of experience finishing V/VVIP aircraft cabinetry and interior components.

• Prior lead or supervisory experience in a finishing, completions, or MRO environment.

• Experience with quality audits, root cause corrective action, or continuous improvement methods such as Lean or 5S.

Supervisory Responsibilities

• This position does not have formal direct reports or hiring and firing authority. The Finish Shop Lead directs and coordinates the daily work of finish shop personnel, provides on-the-job training and coaching, and provides input to the Finish Shop Supervisor on performance and development.

Knowledge, Skills, and Other Attributes

• Complete coating system knowledge, from surface preparation through primers, sealers, stains, basecoats, and topcoats.

• Paint chemistry fundamentals, including mix ratios, catalysts, reducers, pot life, flash, and cure.

• Advanced spray application and color matching skills.

• Skill in finish defect investigation and correction.

• Ability to interpret technical specifications and engineer-supplied data.

• Production planning and workflow coordination.

• Material ordering and inventory control.

• Understanding of quality standards and audit practices.

• Team leadership, with the ability to coach and develop others.

• Process improvement and structured problem-solving, including root cause analysis.

• High attention to detail and commitment to finish quality.

Working Conditions

• Work is performed primarily in the Finish Shop and paint/spray booths, with periodic work in the Cabinet Shop, aircraft hangars, and on or around aircraft.

• Involves regular exposure to coatings, catalysts, solvents, adhesives, sanding dust, and fumes; required PPE, including respiratory protection, must be worn.

• Requires the ability to distinguish variations in color, shade, and gloss to perform color matching and finish inspection.

• Considered MEDIUM work with frequent lifting up to 20 lbs and occasional lifting up to 50 lbs; involves prolonged standing and repetitive arm and hand motion during spraying and sanding; may require climbing ladders and using lifts.

• Travel not typically required; may occur on occasion for offsite support, AOG support, or training.

• May require flexible shifts, overtime, weekends, or holidays based on project demand.

Safety-Sensitive Position

As part of the hiring process, applicants who receive an offer of employment will be asked to submit to a screening test to detect the presence of drugs (marijuana, opiates, cocaine, amphetamines, phencyclidine/PCP). Offers of employment are conditioned on a negative result. If you are asked to submit to a drug test and you refuse to be tested, or you do not pass, Citadel Aviation, LLC. will revoke any offer of employment. All drug tests will be conducted in accordance with applicable federal and state law.

Type One Energy is looking for a motivated Fusion Engineering Summer Intern to support experimental research and development within our Fuel Cycle and Ceramic Breeder teams.

The intern will help investigate how hydrogen and its isotopes interact with materials relevant to fusion energy systems, with particular emphasis on the use of hydrogen and deuterium as non-radioactive surrogates for tritium. This work will contribute to our understanding of hydrogen transport, retention, and release in candidate materials for fusion fuel-cycle and ceramic breeder applications.

Working alongside experienced engineers and scientists, the intern will gain practical laboratory experience while contributing to experimental investigations and supporting computational modelling activities.


Key responsibility could include:

  • Assist in the planning, preparation, and execution of laboratory experiments investigating hydrogen and deuterium interactions with materials.
  • Support experimental testing of candidate ceramic breeder materials and other materials relevant to fusion fuel-cycle systems.
  • Help develop and test hypotheses relating to hydrogen transport, diffusion, retention, and release under different experimental conditions.
  • Gain hands-on experience with laboratory equipment, experimental instrumentation, gas-handling systems, and materials characterization techniques.
  • Collect, process, and analyse experimental data, identifying trends and comparing results with expected material behaviour.
  • Assist in developing simple computational models and analytical tools to support experimental interpretation and improve understanding of hydrogen–material interactions.
  • Document experimental procedures, results, and findings, and communicate progress to the wider engineering team.
  • Contribute to maintaining a safe, organized, and effective laboratory environment by following established procedures and safe working practices.

What you'll need:

  • Pursuing a bachelor’s program in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Physics, or a closely related discipline.
  • A fundamental understanding of materials science, thermodynamics, heat and mass transfer, or related engineering principles.
  • An interest in experimental research, laboratory testing, and hands-on engineering activities.
  • Some experience with data analysis, programming, or engineering calculations through coursework, laboratory classes, or personal projects.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail.
  • Willingness to learn new experimental techniques, computational tools, and laboratory procedures.
  • Ability to communicate technical concepts and experimental findings clearly in written and verbal form.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous laboratory experience through university coursework, research projects, or internships.
  • Familiarity with Python, MATLAB, or similar tools for data analysis and basic computational modelling.
  • Coursework or project experience involving materials characterization, diffusion, mass transfer, or hydrogen-related technologies.
  • Familiarity with experimental instrumentation, data acquisition, or gas-handling systems.
  • Interest in fusion energy, hydrogen technologies, advanced materials, or nuclear engineering.

Type One Energy applies proven advanced manufacturing methods, modern computational physics and high-field superconducting magnets to develop its optimized stellarator fusion energy system. Our FusionDirect development program pursues the lowest-risk, shortest-schedule path to a fusion power plant over the coming decade, using a partner-intensive and capital-efficient strategy.

Type One Energy is committed to community engagement in the development and deployment of its clean energy technology. For more information, visit or follow us on LinkedIn.

Our Mission

The mission of Portage Learning is to transform lives and communities by providing learning opportunities for all who aspire to thrive. We do this not only through superior online instruction but with a deep commitment to expanding access to education. We believe service is the thread that binds our community and our team together. To that end, we choose to …

  • Believe the best in our employees
  • Invest in our people
  • Collaborate with humility, respect, and appreciation
  • Cultivate curiosity and encourage creativity

A Place Where Creativity and Curiosity Matter

Portage Learning is developing a new 100-level, fully online, asynchronous Introduction to Information Technology course for undergraduate students, introductory IT and Computer Science majors, and general education students seeking fundamental technology literacy. We are seeking a Subject Matter Expert to author comprehensive module content, create aligned assessments, and collaborate with our Instructional Design team to build an engaging, standards-aligned course.


The SME will develop 8 modules that cover an Introduction to IT. The course will provide students with a broad introduction to information technology and the technologies that support modern computing and organizations. Major areas of study will include computer hardware and software, networking and Internet infrastructure, cloud computing, cybersecurity and data privacy, databases, programming and computational thinking, and enterprise information systems. Students will also explore emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things, along with ethical considerations and career pathways within the IT field. The course will combine foundational concepts with introductory hands-on experiences in areas such as networking, databases, cybersecurity, and Python scripting.


The SME may also have the opportunity to be contracted for teaching the course through on camera delivery.


What You’ll Invest In:

The Intro to IT Course Author will:

Course Writing & Content Development

  • Curate and/or write full lesson content for 8 asynchronous modules aligned to course learning objectives.
  • Ensure each module includes clear explanations, examples, and learner-appropriate practice opportunities.
  • Integrate or adapt open educational resources (OERs) where appropriate, following Portage guidelines.
  • Curate or create hands-on experiences in areas such as networking, databases, cybersecurity, etc.

Assessments & Academic Integrity

Create for each module:

  • 1 problem set (20 – 25 questions)
  • 1 module exam
  • 1 lab or simulation experience for student practice
  • Develop question banks with 6 alternate versions per question
  • Assessments relevant to hands-on experiences
  • Align all assessments to CLOs and provide rationale/notes for Academic Data review.

Slides & Multimedia Collaboration

  • Draft lecture slides for each module following Portage production standards.
  • Identify 2–3 “high-value” concepts per module for H5P/interactive reinforcement.
  • Collaborate with Instructional Design, Production, Accessibility, and Editorial teams through iterative review cycles.

Deliverables

  • Final written module scripts/content (per Portage template)
  • Lecture slide decks per module
  • Problem sets, exams, and exam banks
  • Notes for interactive/H5P opportunities
  • Revisions based on internal review feedback

Perform other related duties as assigned.

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential function(s).

title: Member Experience Specialist

Our Member Experience Specialists are the primary point of contact for our members at XYPN. This is a full-time role for a conscientious, kind individual with a passion for creating smiles and delivering smart, thoughtful service, both written and verbal.


This role blends customer service and customer success to ensure our members receive the best possible experience. You’ll support members with prompt, thorough, and warm service they’ll be excited to share with their peers. You’ll also become fluent in our membership offerings, helping members fully maximize their (many!) member benefits.


The ideal candidate will have strong communication skills, be a self-starter, and bring a “don’t stop until I have the answer” mindset. You’ll quickly build a deep understanding of our membership offerings and services and be able to clearly and enthusiastically communicate them to members across video, phone, and email.


What you'll be doing

  • Become an expert in the XYPN membership offering, serving as a primary point of contact for members across multiple support channels and upholding XYPN's communication standards

  • Administration of key internal workflows in Monday.com, including onboarding, offboarding, failed payments, technology administration, and at-risk member outreach

  • Be available for required travel to Bozeman, MT for retreat events (~2x per year) and travel for our annual conference, XYPN LIVE

  • Qualifications
  • Valid CDL Class A License

title: Test Technician Supervisor
description:
About Us:

At Tomball Controls, we specialize in manufacturing custom fuel tanks, custom sound attenuated enclosures, and access platforms for emergency power generators.

We are proud to serve clients across various industries, providing them with high-quality power packaging solutions to meet their specific requirements. With years of experienced team members and a commitment to excellence, we have built a reputation for delivering reliable and durable products on time and within budget.


Job Description:

We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Test Technician Supervisor for our location in Von Ormy, TX (south San Antonio, TX). The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience operating and load testing diesel generator systems, a strong understanding of electrical and mechanical safety, and experience leading technicians in a field-service environment.

The Test Technician Supervisor is responsible for safely leading and performing load bank testing of diesel-powered generator systems in accordance with manufacturer requirements, customer specifications, applicable electrical standards, and company safety procedures.

The Test Technician Supervisor must possess a strong working knowledge of diesel generator operation, electrical distribution systems, load bank connections and operation, generator controls, and electrical and mechanical safety hazards.

A primary responsibility of this position is the continuous monitoring of generator and load bank performance and the ability to recognize abnormal operating conditions that could result in equipment damage, catastrophic failure, fire, electrical incident, or personnel injury.

The Test Technician Supervisor must have the judgment and authority to reduce load, remove load, or immediately terminate a test whenever operating conditions become unsafe or fall outside acceptable parameters. Meeting a testing schedule or completing a test shall never take priority over personnel safety or protection of customer equipment.


Key Responsibilities:


Load Bank Testing

  • Lead and perform load bank testing of diesel-powered generator systems.
  • Review generator nameplate information, manufacturer's requirements, customer specifications, and test procedures before beginning work.
  • Determine appropriate load bank configuration and loading requirements based on generator capacity and test objectives.
  • Safely connect and disconnect load banks using approved cables, cam-locks, lugs, bus connections, or other approved connection methods.
  • Verify correct voltage, phase rotation, frequency, grounding, and connection configuration before applying load.
  • Inspect all temporary connections, cables, terminations, and load bank equipment prior to energizing.
  • Operate load banks and apply load in controlled increments.
  • Continuously monitor generator and load bank operation throughout the test.
  • Record required operating parameters at appropriate intervals.
  • Perform load testing for the required duration and at specified load percentages.
  • Properly unload and shut down the test when testing requirements have been completed or when abnormal conditions are identified.
  • Safely disconnect and secure all temporary testing equipment following completion of the test.

Critical Operating Judgment

The Test Technician Supervisor is responsible for recognizing conditions that indicate a generator or load bank may be operating outside safe or acceptable limits. Recognizing a developing problem and terminating the test before equipment failure occurs is more important than completing the scheduled test.

The Test Technician Supervisor must be capable of identifying warning signs including, but not limited to:

  • Abnormal or rapidly changing voltage.
  • Frequency instability or significant frequency deviation.
  • Excessive or rapidly increasing amperage.
  • Voltage or current imbalance.
  • Unusual changes in generator output.
  • Excessive engine coolant temperature.
  • Rapidly increasing coolant temperature.
  • Low, dropping, or unstable oil pressure.
  • Abnormal fuel pressure or fuel-system indications when monitored.
  • Excessive exhaust temperature when monitored.
  • Abnormal engine noise.
  • Excessive or unusual vibration.
  • Unusual smoke or changes in exhaust appearance.
  • Fuel, oil, coolant, or other fluid leaks.
  • Electrical arcing, sparking, smoke, or burning odor.
  • Overheating cables, lugs, cam-locks, bus connections, or other electrical components.
  • Load bank overheating or abnormal operation.
  • Generator alarms or protective-device indications.
  • Unusual electrical or mechanical sounds.
  • Unexpected changes in engine speed.
  • Any condition indicating potential engine, alternator, switchgear, load bank, or electrical-system failure.

Test Termination Authority

The Test Technician Supervisor has the authority and responsibility to immediately reduce load or terminate a load bank test whenever unsafe or abnormal conditions are observed. The technician must:

  • Understand normal operating characteristics of the generator being tested.
  • Establish acceptable operating parameters before applying load.
  • Continuously compare actual operating conditions against those parameters.
  • Recognize trends that indicate a developing problem before a protective shutdown or catastrophic failure occurs.
  • Reduce load when necessary to stabilize an abnormal condition.
  • Remove load immediately when continued operation could damage equipment or create a safety hazard.
  • Initiate an emergency shutdown when required.
  • Notify the appropriate supervisor, customer representative, or responsible personnel when a test is terminated.
  • Clearly document the reason for terminating the test.
  • Never continue a test solely to satisfy a scheduled load percentage or test duration when equipment operation is questionable.

The Test Technician Supervisor is expected to err on the side of protecting personnel and equipment. When in doubt about the safety or condition of the generator, the appropriate action is to unload and evaluate the situation rather than continue testing.


Electrical Safety Responsibilities

The Test Technician Supervisor must have a thorough understanding of the electrical hazards associated with generator and load bank testing. Responsibilities include:

  • Recognizing electrical shock, arc-flash, arc-blast, and arc-fault hazards.
  • Following applicable OSHA, NFPA 70E, company, and customer safety requirements.
  • Establishing appropriate work boundaries around energized equipment.
  • Using properly rated PPE and electrical test equipment.
  • Verifying equipment status before making or removing connections.
  • Following lockout/tagout procedures when applicable.
  • Confirming absence of voltage before performing work where required.
  • Ensuring proper phase identification and rotation.
  • Ensuring proper grounding and bonding.
  • Inspecting all cables and connections before and during testing.
  • Monitoring connections for excessive heat, discoloration, arcing, or other indications of failure.
  • Maintaining proper separation and routing of temporary power cables.
  • Never bypassing safety devices, protective systems, or load bank interlocks without an approved procedure.

Mechanical and Environmental Safety

The Test Technician Supervisor must recognize hazards associated with operating diesel generators and load bank equipment, including:

  • Rotating engine components.
  • Cooling fans and belts.
  • Hot exhaust systems and engine components.
  • Pressurized cooling systems.
  • Diesel fuel and fuel-system hazards.
  • Lubricating oil and hydraulic pressure hazards where applicable.
  • High-temperature radiator discharge air.
  • Generator vibration.
  • Exhaust gases and carbon monoxide.
  • Fire hazards.
  • Noise exposure.
  • Weather and environmental conditions.
  • Inadequate ventilation.
  • Improperly positioned or secured load bank equipment.

The Test Technician Supervisor must continuously evaluate the work area and stop testing when environmental or mechanical conditions create an unacceptable risk.

Crew Leadership

  • Supervisor assigned technicians during generator load bank testing operations.
  • Conduct or participate in pre-job safety meetings and review the JHA/JSA.
  • Ensure all technicians understand the testing procedure and identified hazards.
  • Assign responsibilities according to technician qualifications and experience.
  • Supervise proper load bank connections and disconnections.
  • Ensure technicians understand expected generator operating parameters and test-termination criteria.
  • Maintain control of the testing operation throughout the job.
  • Stop work when unsafe conditions are identified.
  • Lead by example in all safety practices.
  • Communicate effectively with customers, supervisors, project managers, and other contractors.

Generator and Load Bank Knowledge

The Test Technician Supervisor must demonstrate a working knowledge of:

  • Diesel generator operation.
  • Three-phase electrical systems.
  • Generator voltage and frequency characteristics.
  • Generator nameplate ratings.
  • Load bank ratings and operating requirements.
  • Resistive and reactive load banks when applicable.
  • Load bank connection methods.
  • Generator control panels and basic protective functions.
  • Generator alarms and shutdown systems.
  • Voltage regulation and frequency control.
  • Electrical distribution and temporary power connections.
  • Proper loading and unloading procedures.
  • Normal versus abnormal generator operating conditions.

The Test Technician Supervisor is not necessarily expected to diagnose or repair every generator problem. The technician must, however, be able to recognize when generator performance is abnormal, understand the potential consequences, and take appropriate action to protect personnel and equipment.

Documentation

  • Complete accurate load bank test reports.
  • Record generator identification and nameplate information.
  • Record voltage, amperage, frequency, kW, power factor, and other required readings.
  • Record load percentages and test duration.
  • Document alarms, abnormal conditions, test interruptions, and test termination.
  • Clearly document the reason a test was stopped when applicable.
  • Report equipment concerns to the appropriate personnel.
  • Obtain required customer signatures and complete all required test documentation.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience operating and/or testing diesel generator systems.
  • Demonstrated experience connecting and operating generator load banks.
  • Strong understanding of three-phase electrical systems.
  • Ability to read electrical one-line diagrams and generator documentation.
  • Working knowledge of generator controls and protective functions.
  • Strong understanding of electrical and mechanical safety hazards.
  • Ability to recognize abnormal generator operation and determine when a test should be reduced or terminated.
  • Ability to safely use electrical test instruments.
  • Ability to Test Technician Supervisors in a field-service environment.
  • Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record.
  • Ability to travel to customer sites and work extended hours when required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with industrial diesel generators and generator paralleling systems.
  • Experience with Caterpillar, Cummins, Kohler, Generac, MTU, Detroit, and other major generator manufacturers.
  • Experience with large industrial load banks.
  • Experience with resistive and reactive load banks.
  • NFPA 70E training.
  • OSHA safety training.
  • CPR/First Aid certification.
  • Experience working around medium-voltage electrical equipment.
  • Previous field-service or Test Technician Supervisor experience.

Safety Expectations:

Safety and equipment protection are the highest priorities of this position.

The Test Technician Supervisor is expected to maintain constant awareness of electrical, mechanical, thermal, fire, and environmental hazards throughout the testing process.

The Test Technician Supervisor must understand that generator load testing intentionally places a significant load on equipment and that conditions can change rapidly. The technician must continuously monitor the equipment and be prepared to unload or terminate the test before a developing problem becomes an equipment failure.

The Test Technician Supervisor has the authority and responsibility to STOP THE TEST whenever conditions become unsafe, abnormal, or outside acceptable operating parameters.

No test percentage, test duration, customer request, production schedule, or completion deadline takes priority over the safety of personnel or protection of equipment.

Key Performance Expectations:

A successful Test Technician Supervisor will:

  • Safely perform generator load bank testing.
  • Demonstrate strong knowledge of load bank connections and operation.
  • Understand normal generator operating characteristics.
  • Continuously monitor generator performance during testing.
  • Recognize early warning signs of potential equipment failure.
  • Make sound decisions regarding load reduction and test termination.
  • Prevent avoidable catastrophic equipment failures through proper observation and judgment.
  • Maintain control of the test operation and field crew.
  • Communicate concerns immediately and effectively.
  • Produce accurate and complete test documentation.
  • Protect customer equipment and personnel at all times.
  • Know when to stop the test.

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to work around operating diesel generators and energized electrical equipment.
  • Ability to work outdoors and in industrial, construction, and mechanical environments.
  • Ability to work in hot, cold, wet, dusty, and noisy environments.
  • Ability to climb ladders and stairs.
  • Ability to stand, bend, kneel, crawl, and work in restricted areas.
  • Ability to safely handle heavy electrical cables and testing equipment using appropriate lifting and material-handling procedures.
  • Ability to wear required PPE for extended periods.

Equal Opportunity Employer/Minorities/Women/Veterans/Disabled

  • Tomball Controls is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. Tomball Controls is committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.
